boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Niagara University environments for individual work, group preparation, and project production, with access limits noted where they apply.

cards.title: Our Lady of Angels Library
cards.subtitle: Campus library • Niagara University
cards.notes: Settle in between classes with your materials, then ask library staff about available study rooms and research support for your assignment.
cards.short_summary: The campus library and a documented all-student study option.
cards.evidence_claim: Niagara states that its library and designated study rooms are open to all students.
cards.access_notes: Niagara describes the library as open to all students; confirm day-specific building hours with the library before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Dr. Rita N. Moretti Teachers' Studio
cards.title: Dr. Rita N. Moretti Teachers' Studio
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Our Lady of Angels Library
cards.notes: Use the children’s literature collection and classroom-material tools to develop lesson ideas or build visual materials for an education project.
cards.short_summary: A library studio stocked with teaching and curriculum materials.
cards.evidence_claim: The studio supports teacher candidates with reading materials and equipment, and its materials may be used or borrowed by the Niagara community.
cards.source_title: Dr. Rita N. Moretti Teachers' Studio - Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Located on the library’s second floor; the source says studio materials may be used or borrowed by the Niagara University community.

cards.title: Teachers' Studio Study Room
cards.subtitle: Inside Dr. Rita N. Moretti Teachers' Studio
cards.notes: Bring a focused reading or planning task and use this smaller room when it is vacant; it operates on a first-come, first-used basis.
cards.short_summary: A first-come study room within the library’s Teachers’ Studio.
cards.evidence_claim: Niagara Library documents a small study room within the Teachers' Studio that is available first come, first used.
cards.source_title: Dr. Rita N. Moretti Teachers' Studio - Special Collections
cards.access_notes: First come, first used; located within the second-floor Teachers’ Studio.

cards.title: Teachers' Studio Recording Room
cards.subtitle: Next to the Teachers' Studio, library second floor
cards.notes: Use the soundproofed setup for a narrated presentation, podcast, or video assignment, and check out extra project equipment from Library of Things.
cards.short_summary: A soundproof project room for recorded course work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Recording Room has a computer, microphone, Niagara backdrop, and soundproofing; extra podcasting and video-project materials can be borrowed.
cards.source_title: Dr. Rita N. Moretti Teachers' Studio - Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Located on the left side of the Teachers’ Studio. Confirm availability and any equipment-loan process with the library.

cards.title: Gallagher Center Lower Level
cards.subtitle: Gallagher Center (“Gally”)
cards.notes: Use the lower-level seating for a between-class work session, then keep group members nearby by meeting in the same student-center area.
cards.short_summary: A student-center setting documented for eating, meeting, studying, and relaxing.
cards.evidence_claim: Niagara says the Gallagher Center lower level offers a relaxing atmosphere where students can eat, meet with classmates, study, and relax.
cards.access_notes: Student-center lower level; the source describes it as a student space. Food service is nearby, but a purchase is not stated as required to study.

cards.title: Gallagher Center Multi-Purpose Room
cards.subtitle: Gallagher Center lower level • MPR
cards.notes: Reserve the MPR for a larger project meeting, presentation rehearsal, or student-program work session instead of relying on walk-in availability.
cards.short_summary: A reservable large-format room for meetings and presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: Niagara identifies the MPR as a community meeting space for large meetings and lectures and says reservations use the Ad Astra scheduling system.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required through Ad Astra; contact Campus Activities with questions. It may be programmed for events.

cards.title: Student Clubs & Organizations Office Lounge
cards.subtitle: Gallagher Center lower level
cards.notes: If you are preparing club work, use the office’s lounge and computers while coordinating with your organization’s officers or scheduled meeting needs.
cards.short_summary: A club-oriented work area with computers and a lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Niagara says the Student Clubs & Organizations Office includes computers and a lounge area and serves as home base for student clubs and organizations.
cards.access_notes: Designed as a home base for student clubs and organizations; verify access with the Student Clubs & Organizations Office.

cards.title: O'Shea Hall First-Floor Study Room
cards.subtitle: O'Shea Hall residence hall
cards.notes: For residents, use the dedicated study room when you need a change from your room; pair a work block with the first-floor lounge amenities.
cards.short_summary: A residence-hall study room alongside a renovated first-floor lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Niagara describes O’Shea Hall as having a first-floor lounge with new furniture and a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in O’Shea Hall, a residence hall; intended access is for hall residents and should be confirmed with Residence Life.

cards.title: O'Shea Hall Floor Study Lounges
cards.subtitle: O'Shea Hall residence hall
cards.notes: Use the study lounge on your floor for a quick reading session or quiet assignment work without leaving the residence hall.
cards.short_summary: One study lounge is documented on each O’Shea floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Niagara states that each floor of O’Shea Hall has its own study lounge for students to use.
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall space; intended for O’Shea residents. Check Residence Life guidance for guest and building access rules.

cards.title: Seton Hall First-Floor Study Tables
cards.subtitle: Seton Hall residence hall
cards.notes: Use the first-floor study tables for a shared problem set or reading block, keeping your materials compact around the lounge’s common-use setup.
cards.short_summary: Study tables in Seton’s large first-floor residence-hall lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Niagara lists new study tables among the features of Seton Hall’s large first-floor lounge.
cards.access_notes: Located in Seton Hall, a residence hall; intended access is for hall residents and should be confirmed with Residence Life.
